evidence.title: Jakarta Post: Freeport's Gresik smelter halts operations for furnace repairs
evidence.excerpt: PT Freeport Indonesia halted the Gresik smelter over operational issues requiring urgent furnace repairs, effective 8 August and announced on 13 August. President Director Tony Wenas told Bisnis.com the repairs are projected to be completed in Q3 2026 and that the suspension does not affect Grasberg production, with sales timing under review. The plant, built in 1996 and 34% held by Mitsubishi Materials, runs 342,000 t/yr of cathode from Grasberg concentrate.

evidence.title: TechTimes: Indonesia smelter failure extends copper record rally as global stockpiles near crisis
evidence.excerpt: Frames the outage as a supply event: copper futures held near a record 6.61 dollars a pound on 11 August, five days after a COMEX all-time high of 6.7045, with the Gresik failure named as extending the rally. This is the framing the round's narrative call said the trade press would not use.

evidence.title: Reuters via Mining.com: Indonesia copper shipments delayed by Gresik smelter outage
evidence.excerpt: On 8 August PT Smelting's Gresik smelter went offline after a water leak from a boiler; buyers were told the plant would stay closed for checks and repairs over the coming weeks. The plant is jointly owned by Freeport Indonesia and Mitsubishi Materials, has 342,000 t/yr of cathode capacity and processes Grasberg concentrate exclusively. Read through the search summary: the page itself returns 403 to the fetcher.

evidence.title: Shanghai Metals Market: PT Smelting Gresik sudden accident, SMM analysis
evidence.excerpt: Trade-desk analysis treating the stoppage as a near-term tightening of regional refined copper availability against already constrained concentrate supply, with regional premiums the transmission. Again a supply framing rather than a repair framing.

evidence.title: Daily closes for 5711.T, FCX, AMMN.JK, 8058.T, SCCO and ANTO.L around 8 August 2026 (read through the harness price carrier)
evidence.excerpt: Mitsubishi Materials closed -0.77%, +3.59% and +0.48% on 10, 12 and 13 August inside a 4.84% band. Freeport closed +0.39, -3.18, -0.37, -4.30 and -1.38% across the five sessions inside a 4.90% band. Amman stayed inside a 7.1% band. Every called leg stayed inside its own band. The complex fell together on 13 August, the announcement day, and only Antofagasta - a chain-hop leg on another node - closed outside its band.

evidence.title: Fastmarkets: Freeport declares force majeure at Grasberg after the mud rush (recorded as a confound, not as evidence in the window)
evidence.excerpt: The Grasberg Block Cave mud rush of 8 September 2025 killed seven workers and led Freeport to declare force majeure on Indonesian shipments later that month, with output curbed into 2026. Recorded here because a search for force majeure in this round's window returns it: it is a prior-year event on the mine, not a declaration on the smelter outage, and must not be read into the thirty-day window.

resolutions.scorer_note: Scored early because the settling fact is final: the operator's own announcement of 13 August calls it 'operational issues requiring urgent furnace repairs' and names furnace damage. The call said a repairable utility failure rather than damage to the furnace line, and reasoned from the word boiler in the prompt. The second limb held (Q3 completion, a partial-quarter framing, no effect on Grasberg production), but the first limb is the map and it was wrong. This is the fourth map call lost to a document the operator could not or did not read at lock: the settling document here was the owner's own statement, which did not exist until day five, and v14 C3 recorded the attempt and the failure rather than letting it pass silently.

The narrative row is due first and is scored first, and it lost. TechTimes on 11 August ran the outage as extending a record copper rally; SMM read it as a near-term tightening of regional refined availability working through premiums; Reuters led on delayed shipments. Not one first-week account framed it as a routine utility repair. The baseline (any smelter outage is reported as a supply story) had it, and had it plainly.

Mitsubishi Materials closed -0.77%, +3.59% and +0.48% on 10, 12 and 13 August, inside its own 4.84% pre-event band on every session, including the day its partner announced the halt. No carrier attributes a move at 5711 to the outage. The visibility ratio operated as cited, and the stake term said so numerically at lock: 1.5% of impact against a 4.84% band is 0.26, a quarter of appetite.

Freeport closed +0.39, -3.18, -0.37, -4.30 and -1.38% across the five sessions, inside its 4.90% band throughout. Stated confound, and it is the interesting part of the round: the whole copper complex fell together on 13 August (SCCO -3.49%, ANTO -6.83%, AMMN -3.95%), so there was a real move on the announcement day and every band was wide enough to swallow it. Nothing attributes FCX's move to Gresik rather than to the complex.

Amman closed inside its 7.1% band on all five sessions (-1.22, -3.27, +2.27, -3.95, +0.64%). The competitor did not rise on a rival's outage, which is what the call said and the opposite of the baseline. The band is wide because the listing is volatile, which is the same qualification this programme keeps having to write: an absence call on a name that moves 7% on ordinary days is cheap.

Day five. PT Freeport Indonesia's president director confirmed the halt publicly on 13 August and named Q3 2026 for the repairs, and buyers had already been told at the event that the plant would be closed for weeks. The seeded base rate (18 of 20 that a listed party confirms a step within five days) was the right denominator, cited, and not departed from.

No force majeure on concentrate offtake or cathode delivery from this outage appears in any carrier read inside thirty days. Scored thin, and with the confound named rather than left in the search results: a Grasberg force majeure does exist in the record, from the mud rush of 8 September 2025, and a careless search returns it inside this window. It is a prior-year declaration on the mine, not on the smelter stoppage. The base rate (6 of 20) pointed the right way, and a repair covered by stock is the case it describes.
